rules.text: Flag (do not auto-deny) an email found in a breach corpus — exposure alone is not misconduct; corroborate with Hashcrack before denying.
Deny any candidate whose claimed GitHub does not match their commit email history.
Deny any candidate who behaves hostilely or threatens the service.
Deny any candidate whose submitted logs show brute-force activity from their account.
Deny any candidate who submits an image with a covert embedded payload.
Deny any candidate whose logs show a credential-stuffing sweep (one source hitting many accounts).
Deny any candidate whose logs reveal a low-and-slow intrusion spread to evade detection.
Deny any candidate who submits an image hiding an encrypted/obfuscated payload.
Deny any candidate whose submitted credential cracks to a password found in a known breach corpus.
Deny any candidate still submitting a credential whose plaintext recurs across multiple breach corpora.
Deny any candidate submitting an unsalted / plaintext-equivalent credential — it cracks on the first attempt.
Deny any candidate whose handle matches a known threat / dark-web forum account.
Flag (do not auto-deny) a claimed connection IP that does not match the submitted logs — corroborate before denying.
Flag (do not auto-deny) a weakly-encrypted credential that cracks to a weak password — poor hygiene, not proof of malice.
